text:
Rancho del Abuelo / Mendiola Arregui

Rancho del Abuelo is an equestrian complex located in Jalisco, on the outskirts of Guadalajara. Its program coordinates spaces dedicated to the sheltering and care of horses with others designed for resting, gathering, and contemplation, establishing different ways of living and engaging with the landscape and equestrian life.

title: House in Vinhedo / Apiacás Arquitetos
text:
House in Vinhedo / Apiacás Arquitetos

The flat terrain with generous dimensions, intended for a residence with a maximum area of 250 m², motivated us to position it in a way to maximize the interface between the covered program and the external areas. The resulting distribution follows a logic already tested in other residential projects by the office, where the circulation between the rooms is configured as covered passages, yet open laterally — without frames or masonry — to extend the experience between the interior and exterior.

text:
Hotel MS Collection Arouca / MiMool Arquitectura & Design de Interiores

The rehabilitation of the former Monastery of Santa Maria de Arouca, classified as a National Monument since 1910, proposes the transformation of a significant part of the monastic complex into a five-star hotel, integrated into the REVIVE program. Rather than a mere functional adaptation, the project stands as an exercise in historical continuity, where architecture, memory, and landscape articulate into a new narrative of use and permanence.

title: AEME Building / Paz Arquitectura
text:
AEME Building / Paz Arquitectura

AEME is a building located in Guatemala City. It has an open floor plan on the first floor dedicated to commercial use and restaurants, a second floor that combines commerce and offices, and three floors exclusively dedicated to offices. The first floor is connected to the street through a double-height entrance with the purpose of emphasizing the opening towards a friendly urban use, with an aim to allow the first floor to be interpreted as an extension of the public space.

title: Rotiers - Renovation of 46 housing units in Brussels  / MULTIPLE Architecture & Urbanism
text:
Rotiers - Renovation of 46 housing units in Brussels / MULTIPLE Architecture & Urbanism

The Rotiers project aims to give a renewed architectural identity to a 1960s social housing building while preserving the qualities of its setting. Located at the edge of the Sonian Forest and surrounded by mature trees, the building is renovated in close relation to its landscape. The intervention addresses several scales, from the building's integration into the neighborhood to the everyday experience of residents and neighbors, with particular attention to the dwellings, shared outdoor spaces, and entrances.

title: Include Enable Connect
text:
Include Enable Connect

Include Enable Connect captures hcma's evolving framework for maximizing social impact through design.
It represents a body of work developed by hcma over many years, and draws on the thinking and experience of our leadership group and project teams, conversations with collaborators and communities, and a wide field of academic research.
Written for architects, project teams, and building operators, it offers a structured way to move from intention to action so we can think more clearly about the social role of the places we create.
At its heart, it's about using design as a tool to support connection, wellbeing, and lasting civic life.

title: From Coastal Reclamation to Data Centers: How India's Architecture Grows Around Water
text:
From Coastal Reclamation to Data Centers: How India's Architecture Grows Around Water

Architecture has treated water either as a backdrop or a problem: a view to be framed, a hazard to be drained, or a utility to be connected. In contemporary India, a more consequential relationship takes shape. Water remains a shared ecological resource, yet the land and infrastructure around it are increasingly financed and defended as economic assets. Coastlines are extended to carry traffic and lake edges become lucrative development zones. The decision to do so passes through multiple institutions with different vocabularies, thereby challenging who determines how water and its surroundings are used, and who faces the consequences.

title: Linden House / Schemata Architects
text:
Linden House / Schemata Architects

The Dromgariff Rainforest is a project led by Bryan and Tara Meehan to regenerate its gardens and forest. One of Ireland's last ancient oak wood rainforests and a protected Special Area of Conservation, the forest stretches across the south of Ireland. The site was once home to Roche's Royal Hotel and its gardens. Although the hotel was lost, traces of its former landscape remain within the forest, including stone steps, terraces, stone walls, and a garden known as the Rockery.

title: From Atoms to Universes: The Architecture of Everything in the Age of AI
text:
From Atoms to Universes: The Architecture of Everything in the Age of AI

AI has become a consumer product faster than it has become a discipline. Each week brings new models and more information than anyone can absorb, and the easy response is uncritical consumption. Architecture needs a different strategy, built on criticism and method. AI is now acquiring spatial intelligence, the capacity to understand how physical space behaves, and architects can test a project against its environment while they design it. Used with judgment, AI can bring architects closer to nature and its complexity, and make them better builders. We simulate the world to learn how to inhabit it.

title: World Cities Day 2026 Explores "Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All"
text:
World Cities Day 2026 Explores "Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All"

On October 31, World Cities Day 2026 will be observed under the theme "Regenerating the City: Adequate Housing for All." Hosted in Fuzhou, China, this year's global observance focuses on how urban regeneration can advance access to adequate housing by improving existing neighborhoods, infrastructure, and public spaces. According to the United Nations, up to 3.4 billion people worldwide lack access to adequate housing, secure tenure, basic services, or affordable living conditions. This challenge points to the need for approaches that consider housing alongside the wider conditions of urban life, including environmental resilience, connectivity, and access to essential services.

title: London’s Oxford Street Opens Its First Traffic-Free Phase
text:
London’s Oxford Street Opens Its First Traffic-Free Phase

In 2016, Mayor of London Sadiq Khan first expressed the intention to pedestrianize Oxford Street, located in the City of Westminster in central London. The original plan was to complete the project in 2020, but after two public consultations, the project was blocked in 2018. Resumed in 2024, it was followed by two public consultations that showed majority support among respondents. Final approval was granted in February 2026, and on Monday, October 26, almost a kilometer, from Orchard Street to Great Portland Street, became traffic-free. This milestone marks the first phase of the program: the section is now closed to private motorized vehicles, buses, taxis and private hire vehicles, cycles, scooters and pedicabs.

title: Modern Architecture in Bahia: Climate and Culture in the Work of Assis Reis
text:
Modern Architecture in Bahia: Climate and Culture in the Work of Assis Reis

Last October 24th marked the centenary of the birth of Brazilian architect Francisco de Assis Couto Reis (1926–2011), who lived and built most of his work in the city of Salvador, Bahia. Assis Reis, as he was better known, had a career shaped not only by the buildings he designed but also by his urban renewal proposals, his design for the Brazilian Pavilion at the World Expo in Osaka, Japan (unbuilt), and the Scale Model of the City of Salvador, landmarked in 2020. His vast and diverse body of work belongs to a specific moment of modern expression in Brazil, when architects of this "second generation" were particularly concerned with adapting to local climatic, geographical, and cultural conditions.

title: Vaastavya Residence / Space Agency
text:
Vaastavya Residence / Space Agency

On a compact urban plot, Vaastavya transforms the limitations of a dense neighborhood into an opportunity to explore vertical living, controlled privacy, and spaces shaped around a family's creative life. Designed for a three-generation family, the residence replaces an aging family home while retaining the clients' desire for a warm, simple, and personal environment. Vageesh Hegde and Sindhu, both working in the software industry, envisioned a home centered around togetherness rather than rigidly separated private spaces.

title: Photography Studio as Local Infrastructure / ArchTank
text:
Photography Studio as Local Infrastructure / ArchTank

Following severe flood damage, a long-standing local photo studio in Japan was demolished and reconstructed as a contemporary civic space integrating a café, observatory, and retail functions. Rather than treating the studio as a closed commercial facility, the project reinterprets the Japanese neighborhood photo studio as a form of social infrastructure connected to local memory, everyday life, and public interaction.

title: House in Ibiza, The Roca Views / Fran Silvestre Arquitectos
text:
House in Ibiza, The Roca Views / Fran Silvestre Arquitectos

Can we build on this hillside by placing a single element upon it? In response to this question, the project is conceived as a very thin plane, just 15 centimetres thick, which folds along the natural slope of the terrain while simultaneously responding to the constraints of the regulations.
